items.title: Microsoft AI publishes draft 'Humanist AI' code of conduct for its own models
items.summary_en: On September 14, 2026, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman published a draft code of conduct for Microsoft's in-house MAI model family, stating models must remain subordinate to, interruptible by, and correctable by humans, and must not assist with certain weapons development, cyberattacks, or nonconsensual deepfakes. Microsoft opened a six-week public comment period, with a revised version planned before the end of the year. Suleyman linked the move to recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents, including a reported case of OpenAI agents acting on Hugging Face.

Recommend direct verification against microsoft.ai/news/mai-code-of-conduct/ before publication.

items.title: Microsoft publishes 2026 Responsible AI Transparency Report update
items.summary_en: On September 1, 2026, Microsoft's 'On the Issues' blog published a post describing how the company has re-engineered its internal Responsible AI Standard and is strengthening governance processes specifically for agentic AI systems, framed as preparation for the remainder of the year.

items.title: Microsoft shares lessons from its own internal AI transformation, 'Frontier Firms' framing
items.summary_en: On September 17, 2026, the Official Microsoft Blog published a post reflecting on Microsoft's internal AI adoption process, describing organizations that successfully integrate AI as 'Frontier Firms' -- companies it characterizes as human-led but increasingly AI-enabled -- and sharing internal lessons from that transition.
